title: Universal evaluation maps for a binomial monoid-algebra tensor ring
statement: Let $R$ be any commutative monoid, written additively, $b\in R$, $A$ a commutative ring and $\beta:R\to(A,\cdot)$ a monoid homomorphism, so $\beta(0)=1$ and $\beta(r+s)=\beta(r)\beta(s)$. Let $Q_b$ be the quotient of $\mathbf N^2\oplus R$ by the monoid congruence generated by $((1,1),0)\sim(0,b)$, with canonical map $g:R\to Q_b$ and branch generators $u,v$. For any commutative monoid $S$, write $\mathbf Z[S]$ for the free abelian group on $[s]$ with $[s][t]=[s+t]$. Give $A$ and $\mathbf Z[Q_b]$ their $\mathbf Z[R]$-algebra structures by $[r]\mapsto\beta(r)$ and $[r]\mapsto[g(r)]$. Put $D=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q_b]$, using the module tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(\lambda\otimes z)(\mu\otimes w)=\lambda\mu\otimes zw$ and $A$-structure $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes[0]$. Write $U_D=1\otimes[u]$ and $V_D=1\otimes[v]$. Then $U_DV_D=\beta(b)\otimes[0]$ and $1\otimes[g(r)]=\beta(r)\otimes[0]$ for every $r\in R$, and $U_D,V_D$ generate $D$ as an $A$-algebra. For every commutative $A$-algebra $C$, with structure map $\iota:A\to C$, and every $x,y\in C$ satisfying $xy=\iota(\beta(b))$, there is a unique $A$-algebra homomorphism $E_{x,y}:D\to C$ with $E_{x,y}(U_D)=x$ and $E_{x,y}(V_D)=y$. It is given on pure monomial tensors by $E_{x,y}(\lambda\otimes[(i,j,r)])=\iota(\lambda)x^iy^j\iota(\beta(r))$. In particular, this formula descends through both the monoid congruence and tensor balancing relations, and any two $A$-algebra homomorphisms out of $D$ agreeing on $U_D,V_D$ are equal. No integrality, finiteness or saturation condition is imposed on $R$.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathbf Z[R]$ and $T=\mathbf Z[Q_b]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to the given commutative $B$-algebras $A,T$. Its clause (1) gives the stated ring structure on the module tensor $D$, and the homomorphisms $a\mapsto a\otimes[0]$ and $z\mapsto1\otimes z$. In particular $D$ is an $A$-algebra with precisely the multiplication and structure map in the statement.

source.place: ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71 (PDF p. 77), cartesian monoid-algebra square. Agent-written explicit affine-ring calculation; the source omits the universal evaluation calculations.

proof.text: Tensor balancing [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $1\otimes[g(r)]=\beta(r)\otimes[0]$, since the two $[r]\in B$ actions are the given ones. The relation $u+v=g(b)$ in $Q_b$ therefore gives $U_DV_D=1\otimes[u+v]=\beta(b)\otimes[0]$. Each $q\in Q_b$ has a representative $(i,j,r)$ and $[q]=[u]^i[v]^j[g(r)]$, whence $\lambda\otimes[q]=(\lambda\beta(r)\otimes[0])U_D^iV_D^j$. The tensor is generated as a $B$-module by pure tensors, so every element is a finite sum of pure tensors after absorbing the $B$-coefficients into their $A$-factor. Expanding their $T$-factors in its integer basis shows every element is a finite $A$-linear combination of these monomials. Thus $U_D,V_D$ generate $D$ as an $A$-algebra.

source.place: ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71 (PDF p. 77), cartesian monoid-algebra square. Agent-written explicit affine-ring calculation; the source omits the universal evaluation calculations.

proof.text: Given $C,\iota,x,y$ as in the statement, define $f(i,j,r)=x^iy^j\iota(\beta(r))$ on $\mathbf N^2\oplus R$. Commutativity of $C$ and multiplicativity of $\beta$ give $f(0,0,0)=1$ and $f(i+i',j+j',r+r')=f(i,j,r)f(i',j',r')$. The relation $f(s)=f(t)$ is an equivalence relation preserved by addition, since $f(s+w)=f(s)f(w)$; it contains the defining pair because $f(1,1,0)=xy=\iota(\beta(b))=f(0,0,b)$. It therefore contains the generated congruence (the intersection of all congruences containing that pair). Consequently $\bar f([(i,j,r)])=f(i,j,r)$ is independent of representative and is a monoid map $Q_b\to(C,\cdot)$. This proves descent through the entire congruence, not only the displayed relation.

source.place: ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71 (PDF p. 77), cartesian monoid-algebra square. Agent-written explicit affine-ring calculation; the source omits the universal evaluation calculations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-integer-monoid-algebra-universal-property] to $M=Q_b$ and $\bar f$. It gives a unital ring homomorphism $h:T\to C$ with $h([(i,j,r)])=x^iy^j\iota(\beta(r))$. Let $\alpha:B\to A$ be the specified coefficient map and $\gamma:B\to T$ the specified base map. On each basis element $[r]$, $h(\gamma([r]))=\iota(\beta(r))=\iota(\alpha([r]))$. Both composites are additive and preserve integer multiples, so their equality on an arbitrary finite integer basis expansion proves $h\gamma=\iota\alpha$. Thus $h$ is a $B$-algebra homomorphism when $C$ has its $B$-structure through $A$.

source.place: ILO Expose VI, Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71 (PDF p. 77), cartesian monoid-algebra square. Agent-written explicit affine-ring calculation; the source omits the universal evaluation calculations.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] with base ring $B$, new base $A$, original algebra $T$ and target $C$. The $B$-algebra map $h$ of step 4 gives an $A$-algebra map $E_{x,y}:D\to C$, with $E_{x,y}(\lambda\otimes z)=\iota(\lambda)h(z)$. At $z=[(i,j,r)]$ this is the required formula, and at $[u],[v]$ it gives $x,y$. Explicitly, for any $t\in B$, $h(\gamma(t)z)=\iota(\alpha(t))h(z)$ by step 4, so the formula takes $(\lambda\alpha(t))\otimes z$ and $\lambda\otimes\gamma(t)z$ to the same value. Additivity in both factors and preservation of integer multiples handle all additive tensor relations. This also verifies the asserted tensor balancing directly.

proof.text: Every $A$-algebra homomorphism $H:D\to C$ sends the monomial expression in step 2 to $\iota(\lambda\beta(r))H(U_D)^iH(V_D)^j$. If $H(U_D)=x$ and $H(V_D)=y$, this equals the displayed formula for $E_{x,y}$; finite addition gives equality on every element of $D$. More generally, any two such homomorphisms agreeing on $U_D,V_D$ have equal values on every monomial in step 2 and hence on their finite $A$-linear combinations. This proves uniqueness and the final assertion. All calculations used only commutative monoid and ring laws; no cancellation, integrality, finiteness or saturation of $R$ is involved.
